full_judgment:
10. Being aggrieved by this judgment and order of the High Court Division the contesting defendants filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1342 of 2006 before this Division and leave was granted to consider the submissions of the learned Counsel for the leave-petitioners to the effect that both the trial court as well as the appellate court below, upon proper consideration of evidence on record, dismissed the suit and there is nothing on record to show that the findings of the courts below are shockingly perverse or are vitiated by non-reading of the material evidence or misconstruction of any important documents affecting the merit of the suit and that the High Court Division upon mere surmise and conjecture held that since the lessees are in unauthorized possession the government is under legal obligation to restore possession of the suit land to the plaintiff Nos. 1 to 6 after evicting the lessees therefrom; that the High Court Division committed error of law in holding that no notice was served upon the plaintiff No. 1 and the defendant Nos. 7 and 8 under the provision of section 92 (3) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 in Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1998-99 overlooking the Exhibit-ঞ, the record of the proceeding of said Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1998-99 and that the High Court Division, without controverting the findings of the courts below to the effect that notice of the said Miscellaneous case was duly served upon the plaintiff No. 1 and that there is no evidence to prove that the co-sharers of SA Khatian No. 330 resides in this country, erroneously held that the suit land was illegally declared as government khas land under section 92 (2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 in Miscellaneous Case No 1 of 1998-99. 

 13. Mr Qumrul Haque Siddique, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-respondents, on the other hand, has made submission to the effect that the original copy of the sale certificate, the Exhibit-4, proves that the suit land was sold in auction in the year 1962 and the possession of this land also was delivered in favour of the auction purchasers, that the contesting defendants though has claimed that this auction sale of the suit land in Certificate Case No. 358 of 1961-62 is collusive, fraudulent, but they could not produce any iota of evidence before court to substantiate this claim that the suit land was sold in auction by the government and the government mutated also the name of the auction purchasers in SA Khatian of the suit land and also received rents from the auction purchasers and granted rent receipts in favour of them regularly upto 1981 and in the circumstances the government now cannot say that the suit land, being escheat property, has vested in the government under section 92 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The learned Advocate has argued that in this suit the contesting defendants did not state anything as to who were owners of the suit land and which of the owners of the suit land died leaving no heir and as to how the suit land became escheat property; that the government did not say anything as to what happened and when did it happen which authorized the government to invoke the powers of section 92 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 to declare the suit land as khas land of the government. The learned Advocate has argued that the government itself allowed the plaintiffs to purchase the suit land in auction in the year 1962 and thereafter mutated the name of the plaintiffs in respect of the suit land in SA Khatian and accepted rent from the plaintiffs for the suit land for a long time since 1962 and also granted rent receipts to the plaintiffs and in the circumstances the government cannot say now that the suit land became escheat property and, as such, it was made khas land of the government rightly. The learned Advocate for the plaintiff-respondents has argued that the High Court Division, on meticulous examination of the evidence and other materials on record and on consideration of all aspects rightly set-aside the findings and decision of the courts below and rightly decreed the suit in part.
